about.title: Citrus Heights Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing someone suddenly leaves a family with more questions than anyone should have to carry. In Citrus Heights, Sacramento County's public collision records for 2025 list 310 injury crashes, 408 people hurt, and 3 lives lost. Behind that last number are three people who each had a household, a routine, a seat at the table. Many of the city's reported collisions cluster along Greenback Lane, Antelope Road, Auburn Boulevard and Sunrise Boulevard, and the busiest window tends to fall on Wednesday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. A wrongful death claim is a civil matter, separate from anything the district attorney may pursue, and California limits who can bring it: a spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The clock runs two years from the date of death, and shorter when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Citrus Heights families, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Citrus Heights Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California gives standing first to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children, then to certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Families generally have two years from the date of death, but that window shrinks when a city, county or state agency is involved. Getting connected sooner protects your options.

items.title: Losses that are actually recoverable
items.desc: A civil claim can address funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. It proceeds independently of any criminal case.

items.question: The crash happened on Greenback Lane and the other driver was cited. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, the two are separate tracks. A citation or criminal charge is handled by prosecutors and does not compensate your family for funeral costs, lost support, or the loss of companionship. A wrongful death claim is the civil action that addresses those losses, and it can move forward regardless of how the criminal matter ends.

items.question: How long do we have to act in California?
items.answer: In most cases the deadline is two years from the date of death. If a public entity such as a city, Sacramento County, or a state agency may share responsibility, a much shorter administrative claim deadline applies. Because of that, it helps to speak with an attorney well before the two-year mark.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge our family anything?
items.answer: No. Our connection service is free, and we are not a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network take wrongful death cases on contingency, which means there is no attorney fee unless your family recovers something.
